headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, yet nothing about today's tape is falling apart
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the whole story before you even get to the daily wiggle: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages. No golden crosses anywhere. That's a market still working through a longer downtrend, full stop, regardless of what the last 24 hours did. BTC sits 48.1% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 60.3% from its high, and the smaller names are worse: ADA is 81.3% off its high, DOGE 75.7%. When every asset agrees on being under trend, that's not noise, that's the map.

But momentum is telling a different, quieter story than trend. BTC's RSI-14 is 55.6 with MACD above signal, a modest bullish tilt inside a downtrend, not a reversal claim, just a rest that's tilted up. ETH and SOL show similar RSI readings in the mid-to-high 50s (56.9 and 57.9) though ETH's MACD sits below signal, a small divergence worth naming: price and short-term momentum aren't fully agreeing even within the same asset. XRP is the outlier to the downside, RSI 37.5, MACD bearish, down 12.45% over 30 days, clearly the weakest tape of the group. This is a market where the trend is down but the momentum gauges aren't confirming further weakness across the board, they're mixed, asset by asset.

Positioning adds texture. BTC funding on OKX is barely positive (0.0004% per 8h, 0.5% annualized), essentially free, no one's paying up to be long. ETH funding is actually negative (-4.1% annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their bets there, an unusual tell in an asset that's up 6.41% over 30 days. Compare that to SOL, XRP, and DOGE, where funding runs hot (7-8% annualized) and long/short ratios are stretched: DOGE's book is 5.2-to-1 long, XRP's is 3.68-to-1 long. Crowded and paying to be long is a more fragile setup than flat and cheap, and BTC's liquidation tape backs that up: of the 531 events in the last 20 hours, $5.24M were shorts wiped out against just $539K of longs, so the squeeze pressure has been on the bears, not the bulls.

The flow picture is constructive without being loud. BTC ETFs posted a net inflow of $297.5M on 17 Aug, though the five-session net is a much smaller $56.9M with same_direction_days at just 1, so don't read a sustained trend into one strong print. ETH ETFs took in $30.9M on the same day, $42.5M over five sessions. Whale wallets moved $29.0M net off exchanges over the last 48 hours, continuing a pattern that shows up in weekly net figures too: two recent weeks of over $1B moving off exchanges, followed by two weeks reversing back onto exchanges (-$407M and -$296M), so even this is not a one-way street lately. Stablecoin float is essentially flat to slightly down (-0.58% over 30 days) at $306.5B, meaning the dry powder on the sidelines isn't growing right now.

Set against all that, the crowd is reading Fear at 41, near the low end of its own 30-day range of 25 to 41. So sentiment sits fearful while BTC funding is near zero, ETH funding is negative, and BTC ETF flows just posted their strongest single day noted here. That gap, fear in the gauge against calm-to-constructive positioning and flow, is the day's real tension, more than any single price move.

What to watch from here: whether BTC can reclaim its 200-day line (it's currently below it despite the RSI/MACD tilt up), whether the five-session ETF net starts agreeing with the daily prints instead of lagging behind them, and whether that weekly whale flow swings back to sustained off-exchange movement rather than alternating direction week to week. Any of those flipping would change the read materially.
